messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - followup

Hi Priya - great to meet today, thanks for walking through the use case. Quick recap and a couple of questions so we can size Dedicated capacity correctly. (Looping in Rafael for sizing/arch.)

Summary of what I heard from the call:
- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and data isolation (Private VPC is a possibility later).
- Primary models: Llama-3 family (we discussed 13B and 70B variants) for chat + retrieval-augmented generation.
- TPS targets: steady-state ~50 TPS, peak burst ~200 TPS for short windows (1-5 min).
- Concurrency: expected 40-60 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Token mix: average prompt tokens ~80, average generation ~180, ~75% short prompts / 25% long-context ops.
- Latency SLO: prefer p95 < 300ms for small prompts, can accept higher for long generations.

Questions / next inputs we need to finalize sizing:
1) Do you have a firm model selection (13B vs 70B) for the initial rollout or will you want both supported?
2) Any hard constraint on cost/GPU SKU preference (A100 vs H100)? We can recommend a mix based on model choice.
3) Can you confirm token mix spikes (are there regular batch jobs that will push long generations)?

Attached is a small capacity_sizing_sheet.xlsx - if you can fill in the expected % of requests by model (13B vs 70B) and any day-of-week peak multipliers, that will help Rafael provide a GPU count estimate and recommended concurrency/batching settings.

Next steps: Rafael will propose GPU SKUs and preliminary node counts once we have the filled sheet. I can schedule a 30-minute sizing call next week to align on the final numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Initial rollout will be primarily 13B for chat (80% of traffic). We expect to add 70B for higher-quality summarization and specialized flows in Q3.
- The 50 TPS steady-state is our conservative estimate; during daytime peak we could see sustained 80-100 TPS for 10-30 minute windows. Bursts to 200 TPS are possible during campaign days.
- Avg tokens you captured look right: prompt ~80, generation ~180. For the heavy summarization jobs the generation side can hit 500-800 tokens but those are ~5% of requests.
- Latency: p95 < 300ms is ideal for chat; for long summarization we can tolerate up to 3s.

Procurement asked to be included on any pricing/terms docs; I cc'd them above.

Thanks for the details - good context. A few notes and an initial recommendation based on the mix you sent:

- For a primarily 13B workload (80%) plus occasional 70B (5-10%), we usually recommend A100 80GB for cost-sensitive customers and H100 80GB if you need best single-request latency for 70B. H100 gives ~20-30% faster p95 on large models but costs more.
- Concurrency / batch sizing: given 40-60 concurrent sessions and average tokens, plan for batching windows around 20-40ms to hit throughput without impacting p95. We can tune batching thresholds by route.
- GPU count (very rough): to meet steady 50-80 TPS with the above mix we estimate ~4-6 A100s (with autoscaling headroom for bursts). If you want to minimize p95 for 70B-heavy flows and reduce token latency, 3-4 H100s would be safer but higher cost.
- For the 200 TPS bursts, we recommend an autoscale buffer (burst capacity) or ephemeral burst pool - this avoids permanently provisioning for peak.

I've attached our redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf with SKU-level pricing and an example node config. If you can confirm the percentage of requests that require long generation (the ~500-800 token jobs), I can give a narrower GPU count.

Proposed next steps:
- Priya/Procurement: confirm whether cost or latency is the primary constraint.
- Priya: share final % of long-generation jobs and any regulatory constraints for Private VPC.
- We'll set up a 30-min sizing call to finalize node counts and autoscale policy.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

- Baseline: 5 x A100 80GB nodes (Dedicated pool) with an autoscale burst option to add up to +3 nodes for campaign peaks.
- Model pinned: start with 13B for launch, add 70B as a separate route once usage is validated.
- Batching: start conservative (20ms batch window) and iterate after observing real traffic for 1-2 weeks.
